item.title: The Standardized Soil Moisture-Temperature Compound Index (SSTCI): daily scale global data set and event catalogue for compound dry-hot extremes (1961–2023)
item.description:
The Standardized Soil Moisture-Temperature Compound Index (SSTCI): daily scale global data set and event catalogue for compound dry-hot extremes (1961–2023)
Rukhshinda Aftab, Daniel Fiifi Tawia Hagan, Guojie Wang, Baoying Shan, Syed Husnain Shah, Zhou Chensi, Wei Xikun, Fareeha Siddique, Ali Hasan Jaffry, and Emmanuel Yeboah
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 7981–8002, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-7981-2026, 2026
This study provides a daily global compound dry–hot index (SSTCI - Standardized Soil Moisture–Temperature Compound Index) for researchers and a ready-to-use CDHE (Compound dry-hot extreme) catalogue for wider users, recording when and where each extreme event occurred, its duration and severity (1961–2023, 0.1°). Built on soil moisture memory and surface air temperature, they show CDHEs have become more frequent and longer lasting in many regions in recent decades, supporting targeted studies of impacts on water, ecosystems and agriculture.

item.title: Updated historical (1750–2023) trends of reactive gases and aerosols from the Community Earth atmospheric Data System (CEDS)
item.description:
Updated historical (1750–2023) trends of reactive gases and aerosols from the Community Earth atmospheric Data System (CEDS)
Rachel Hoesly, Steven Smith, Hamza Ashan, Noah Prime, Patrick O'Rourke, Kalyn Dorheim, Monica Crippa, Zbigniew Klimont, Diego Guizzardi, Leyang Feng, Colin Harkins, Brian C. McDonald, and Shuxiao Wang
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-752,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Here we present an updated historical time series (1750–2023) produced by the Community Earth atmospheric Data System (CEDS), which is widely used in national and international models and modeling exercises. This dataset provides historical estimates of air pollutants and other gases. Aggregate annual estimates are available by 220 countries, 62 sectors, and 8 fuels (in addition to process emissions). Gridded data are also available.

item.title: Ten years of measurements (2012-2022) of the atmospheric composition at Saclay/SIRTA observatory in the Ile de France region as part of ICOS and ACTRIS
item.description:
Ten years of measurements (2012-2022) of the atmospheric composition at Saclay/SIRTA observatory in the Ile de France region as part of ICOS and ACTRIS
Laura Bouillon, Valérie Gros, Morgan Lopez, Nicolas Bonnaire, Carole Philippon, Camille Yver Kwok, Leslie David, Olivier Perrussel, Olivier Sanchez, Simone Kotthaus, Jean-Eudes Petit, Philippe Ciais, and Michel Ramonet
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 7941–7961, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-7941-2026, 2026
The Saclay observatory, 20 km southwest of Paris, monitored greenhouse and reactive gases, as well as aerosols, over 10 years to assess the impact of urban emissions. By comparing downwind and background conditions, the study revealed significant reductions in pollutants linked to traffic: -35.6 % for CO, -52.3 % for NOₓ, -56.7 % for eBC, and -15 % for CO2. These trends align with emission decrease estimates from AIRPARIF inventories over the same period.

item.title: MLAWind: a monthly sea surface wind dataset derived from an interpretable machine learning approach integrating in-situ observations and satellite data
item.description:
MLAWind: a monthly sea surface wind dataset derived from an interpretable machine learning approach integrating in-situ observations and satellite data
Weihao Guo, Rongwang Zhang, Xin Wang, and Dongxiao Wang
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 7963–7979, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-7963-2026, 2026
This study develops a monthly near-global sea surface wind dataset (MLAWind) from 1950–2023 through an interpretable machine learning framework integrating in-situ observations and satellite data. Evaluations show that MLAWind achieves comparable performance to the widely-used reanalysis datasets at different time scales. It provides reliable historical wind data during both satellite and non-satellite periods, demonstrating broad application prospects in ocean and climate research.

item.title: Network-based subbasin-scale mapping of streamflow alteration in Ontario, Canada
item.description:
Network-based subbasin-scale mapping of streamflow alteration in Ontario, Canada
Hongren Shen, Bryan A. Tolson, James R. Craig, Robert A. Metcalfe, Jonathan Romero-Cuellar, and James J. Luce
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 7915–7940, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-7915-2026, 2026
Dams and other water-control structures can influence rivers far downstream. We calculated the Streamflow Alteration Index for 245 576 subbasins across Ontario, Canada, averaging 4.3 square kilometres. By linking structure locations with connected lake and river networks, we mapped potential downstream influence, including places without flow measurements. This province-wide dataset supports river modelling, water management, ecological studies and targeted local assessments.

item.title: A global inventory of rock glaciers
item.description:
A global inventory of rock glaciers
Jinhao Xu, Min Feng, Yanan Su, Dezhao Yan, Qinglin Wu, Peng Zhao, Xuefei Zhang, and Xin Li
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-575,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Rock glaciers are widely distributed in mountain permafrost regions, but existing regional inventories are fragmented, inconsistent, and geographically incomplete, limiting global understanding. We developed the first globally consistent inventory using high-resolution satellite imagery, artificial intelligence, and expert review. This openly available dataset enables global comparisons and supports research on mountain permafrost, water resources, climate change, and environmental change.

item.title: NH-SDN: A Deep Learning-Derived Daily 0.25° Snow Density Dataset for the Northern Hemisphere from 1982–2025
item.description:
NH-SDN: A Deep Learning-Derived Daily 0.25° Snow Density Dataset for the Northern Hemisphere from 1982–2025
Li Zhong, Xueliang Zhang, Yuwen Lin, Dongyang Du, Yixi Bi, Liyang Sun, Yantao Liu, Jiale Geng, Sijie Zhao, and Pengfeng Xiao
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-689,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Snow density is an important property that influences snowpack conditions and their evolution. We created a new daily snow density dataset for the Northern Hemisphere from 1982 to 2025 by combining ground observations, environmental information, and a deep learning framework. The dataset is more accurate than existing products and better captures seasonal and year-to-year changes, providing valuable information for snowpack assessment and climate change research.

item.title: MioTEX: A comprehensive GDGT-based ocean temperature compilation for the Miocene
item.description:
MioTEX: A comprehensive GDGT-based ocean temperature compilation for the Miocene
Alexandra Auderset, Xiaoqing Liu, Neeraj S. Shah, Sarah J. Feakins, Francesca Sangiorgi, Amelia Shevenell, Kasia K. Śliwińska, Appy Sluijs, Evi Wubben, Yi Ge Zhang, Sevasti Modestou, Sindia Sosdian, and Ann Holbourn
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-711,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Climate models struggle to reproduce Miocene (23–5.3 million years ago) ocean temperatures, a period when CO2 levels overlapped near-future projections. Understanding this model–data mismatch requires evaluating available temperature records and uncertainties. We compiled MioTEX, a standardized global dataset of Miocene ocean temperatures from 46 sites using the TEX86 proxy. Calibration choices influence absolute temperatures. MioTEX is freely accessible via an interactive web platform.

item.title: Imaging the Ross Ice Streams of West Antarctica using active source seismology
item.description:
Imaging the Ross Ice Streams of West Antarctica using active source seismology
Huw Joseph Horgan, Andrew Robert Gorman, J. Paul Winberry, Sridhar Anandakrishnan, Howard Conway, Gavin B. Dunbar, Tina van de Flierdt, Denise K. Kulhanek, Richard H. Levy, Molly O. Patterson, and Ilaria Santin
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-723,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Knowledge of the past and future of Earth's ice sheets requires us to image beneath the ice surface and into the ice, water, sediment, and rock that lies beneath. An effective way of doing this uses active source seismology. Here we present active source seismic data imaging a diverse range of subglacial environments including subglacial lakes, sub-ice ocean cavities, and geological archives preserving the history of the ice sheets.

item.title: A long-term gridded dataset of the vegetation–atmosphere decoupling coefficient across the contiguous United States, 1982–2020
item.description:
A long-term gridded dataset of the vegetation–atmosphere decoupling coefficient across the contiguous United States, 1982–2020
Jinran Xiong, Han Chen, Wenli Zhao, Ziqi Lin, Chunmiao Zheng, and Yu Feng
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-732,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Long-term maps showing how vegetation and the atmosphere jointly control water loss from land have been lacking. We present a new dataset for the contiguous United States from 1982 to 2020 by combining observations from 74 field sites with environmental data and a computer model guided by physical principles. The dataset reveals clear differences across regions, seasons, and vegetation types, and includes uncertainty and quality information to support reliable climate, water, and land studies.

item.title: CCWEM and CCWIF: 10 m Datasets of Coastal Wetland Extent and Inundation-Frequency Gradients across China
item.description:
CCWEM and CCWIF: 10 m Datasets of Coastal Wetland Extent and Inundation-Frequency Gradients across China
Jintao Liang, Yong Zhang, Yi Wang, Chao Chen, and Junfan Bao
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-758,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
We provide two open 10 m datasets describing China’s coastal wetlands in 2025. Together, they show both the maximum wetland extent and how tidal inundation varies within wetlands, offering a new national-scale spatial basis for wetland monitoring, ecological research, conservation, restoration, and coastal management.

item.title: A daily gridded dataset of nitrogen wet deposition over East Asia for 2011 to 2016 based on multisource observation-model fusion
item.description:
A daily gridded dataset of nitrogen wet deposition over East Asia for 2011 to 2016 based on multisource observation-model fusion
Nan Yang, Nuohang Liu, Baozhu Ge, Zhechen He, Yin Zhou, Danhui Xu, and Zifa Wang
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-857,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
We developed a daily dataset of nitrogen deposited by precipitation across East Asia for 2011–2016 at a resolution of 45 km. Combining simulations, satellite precipitation data and ground measurements improved agreement with observed daily nitrogen wet deposition. The dataset supports studies of short-lived nitrogen inputs to ecosystems and their contribution to total deposition. It also supports regional nitrogen budget analysis and model evaluation.

item.title: Species- and region-specific growth curves, forest age (2020), and disturbance trends for French forests at 30 m resolution
item.description:
Species- and region-specific growth curves, forest age (2020), and disturbance trends for French forests at 30 m resolution
Agnès Pellissier-Tanon, Yidi Xu, François Ritter, Nikola Besic, and Philippe Ciais
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-864,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
We created open data for mainland French forests to show, for different tree species and regions, how forests grow, how old they are, and how harvest and natural disturbances affect them. Combining satellite biomass and disturbance maps with national forest surveys, we map biomass growth with age, forest age for 2020, disturbance rates and biomass losses, and typical harvest ages. This helps explain the changing forest carbon sink and supports climate and management decisions.
